facts.statement: Hypselorhachis lived during the Middle Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Triassic

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single vertebra found in the Middle Triassic Manda Beds of Tanzania.
facts.quote: It is currently known only from a single vertebra found from the Middle Triassic Manda Beds in Tanzania.

facts.statement: The single known vertebra is slender, measuring only about 20 mm in transverse thickness, though it remains largely intact despite some chipping.
facts.quote: The vertebra is preserved in reasonably good condition, as although the tall neural spine is chipped in several places it is not broken despite being quite slender, only around 20 mm thick transversely.

facts.statement: The type species H. mirabilis was mentioned but never fully described by Alan J. Charig.
facts.quote: The type species is H. mirabilis, mentioned but never fully described by English paleontologist Alan J. Charig.

facts.statement: The name Hypselorhachis translates to 'wonderful high spine', derived from Latin and Greek roots.
facts.quote: The name means 'wonderful high spine', from the Latin 'mirabilis' 'wonderful' and the Greek 'ὑπσελος', 'high' and 'ῥαχις' 'spine' or 'backbone'.

facts.statement: Based on the size of the vertebra, Hypselorhachis was likely at least 3 meters long, possibly reaching 4 or 5 meters.
facts.quote: Hypselorhachis was probably at least 3 metres long, maybe up to 4 or 5 metres, as the vertebra is certainly from quite a large animal.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Lifua Member of the Manda Beds, which dates to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Hypselorhachis is known from a single anterior dorsal vertebra found from the Lifua Member of the Manda Beds, which is thought to have been deposited during the Anisian stage.

facts.statement: The genus is diagnosed by a small dorsal projection on the prezygapophysis of the vertebra.
facts.quote: The only characteristic that diagnoses the genus is a feature seen in the prezygapophysis - a small part of the bone projects dorsally.

facts.statement: The neural spine is approximately 305 mm high, while the centrum is only about 60 mm high.
facts.quote: The neural spine is around 305 mm high, or possibly greater than this as some of the end may be missing, while the centrum is only around 60 mm high even at its tallest points.

facts.statement: The centrum features deeply concave surfaces on its lower, left, and right sides.
facts.quote: As is visible on the picture, the centrum has deeply concave lower, left and right surfaces.

facts.statement: If Hypselorhachis possessed a full sail, it would have been tough because it was composed mostly of transversely compressed bone with little space between the elements.
facts.quote: if, as seems certain, it did have a full sail the sail would have been quite tough due to mostly being transversely compressed bone with little space in between.

facts.statement: The solid and compact neural arch with a thin neural canal suggests the spinal cord was well protected.
facts.quote: The neural arch is very solid and quite compact, and the neural canal rather thin, so the spinal cord would have been relatively well protected.

facts.statement: In 1988, Hypselorhachis was assigned to the family Ctenosauriscidae, a group of sail-backed archosaurs.
facts.quote: Hypselorhachis was assigned to the Ctenosauriscidae, a group of sail-backed archosaurs, in 1988.

facts.statement: Due to the scarcity of fossil material, the current phylogenetic classification of Hypselorhachis remains tentative.
facts.quote: Because of the lack of any other material, comparisons between it and other early archosaurs can only be based on features seen in the vertebra, making any current phylogenetic classification tentative.

facts.statement: Hypselorhachis is classified within the unranked order Paracrocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: unranked_ordo: Paracrocodylomorpha

facts.statement: Hypselorhachis belongs to the superfamily Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: †Poposauroidea

facts.statement: Hypselorhachis is classified in the family Ctenosauriscidae.
facts.quote: familia: †Ctenosauriscidae

facts.statement: The authority for the genus Hypselorhachis is Butler et al., 2009.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Butler et al., 2009

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Hypselorhachis is H. mirabilis.
facts.quote: type_species: †H. mirabilis

facts.statement: The authority for the species H. mirabilis is Butler et al., 2009.
facts.quote: species_authority: Butler et al., 2009

facts.statement: The parent group of Hypselorhachis is the family Ctenosauriscidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ctenosauriscidae

facts.statement: Hypselorhachis is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species for the genus Hypselorhachis is Hypselorhachis mirabilis.
facts.quote: Type species: Hypselorhachis mirabilis

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Hypselorhachis has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
